key_insight: SE-RRMs embed permutation equivariance into Recurrent Reasoning Models so the network inherently respects symbol relabelings, removing the need for costly data augmentation and improving sample efficiency and generalization on symbolic reasoning tasks.
problem_solved: Neural reasoning architectures struggle with symbol symmetries (e.g., relabelings in Sudoku or ARC) and typically require massive data augmentation to learn invariance; this paper addresses that inefficiency by enforcing symmetry in the model itself.
method: Architectural enforcement of permutation equivariance within the RRM family (HRM/TRM) via equivariant layers and tied-weight updates so outputs permute consistently with input symbol relabelings.
Equivariant recurrent/message-passing update rules that preserve symbol symmetry across iterative reasoning steps, keeping representations consistent under permutations.
Evaluation on symbolic reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate reduced augmentation needs, improved sample efficiency, and retention of the compact RRM footprint.
impact: Enforcing symbol equivariance lets practitioners build smaller, more data-efficient reasoning models that generalize across symbol relabelings without heavy augmentation—useful for structured tasks like Sudoku, ARC, and other combinatorial reasoning problems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side architecture diagram: standard RRM with data augmentation vs SE-RRM with built-in equivariant layer.
Schematic showing a permutation of symbols mapping to identical model outputs (illustrates equivariance/invariance).
Bar/line chart comparing accuracy or sample-efficiency: baseline RRM (with augmentation) vs SE-RRM (no augmentation).
Pipeline sketch of recurrent reasoning iterations highlighting equivariant message passing across steps.
paper_authors: Richard Freinschlag, Timo Bertram, Erich Kobler, Andreas Mayr, Günter Klambauer
